# A column lock change during an edit can leave its cells in both bodies

## Context

Two independent sightings, on two different instruments, both on `dev` heads that already carry #18901 and #18909 — so neither of those fixes is the cure:

- **Mine, in CI.** `test/playwright/e2e/grid/CellEditingLockedBodies.spec.mjs`'s `lockEnd` arm went red once: "c3 renders in the end body", received `center`. Every center row had kept a cell for the moved column (`r3c3` after `r3c10`, all 19 rows) while the end body rendered it too. 0 of 136 locally at the time. Broadcast as a defect-note 2026-09-18T17:39Z.
- **@neo-fable's, under a stress recipe, with a worker-side dump.** 1 of 25 and 1 of 25 on two days' heads, dump taken at `dev@61b617a852` while `regionOf(c3)` was still `center` four seconds after the lock change.

Their dump, quoted with its own qualifier — the App Worker is **settled and correct**:

- `columns.get('c3').locked === 'end'`, column order ends `c37, c38, c3, c39`
- center body: 37 fields, `columnPositions.get('c3')` undefined, `mountedColumns [0,9]`
- end body: 2 fields `[c3, c39]`
- every body **and** every row: `isVdomUpdating: false`, `needsVdomUpdate: false` — nothing in the air, nothing queued
- `plugin.session = {dataField: 'c3', held: 0}` — the hold was released

…while the DOM is wrong, and final:

- `c3` cells per body: start 0, **center 19**, end 19; the edited record's center row has 11 cells
- the header is right: the `C3` button sits in the end toolbar only
- one editor

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-09-19T10:33Z; all-state searches for `lost body render`, `column lock change edit`, `grid body stale DOM`; A2A sweep at 10:37Z; Memory Core sweep on the symptom's nouns; own-assignment sweep. Nothing equivalent. The nearest neighbours are #18885 (the *edit* is lost when its column changes body — closed, a different failure) and the #18899 / #18900 / #18901 vdom family (all merged before the measured head).

## The Problem

vdom and vnode agree the center body has no `c3`. The DOM has 19 of them, and **no later render will correct it**, because nothing is queued: from the App Worker's point of view the work is done. The user-facing reading is that after a column lock change during an edit, the grid can show the moved column **twice** — once in the center body and once in its new body — until something unrelated re-renders the center.

**The normal shape, for contrast**, from 110 passing instrumented runs (@neo-fable wrapped `Neo.main.DeltaUpdates.insertNode/moveNode/removeNode/updateNode/replaceChild` and logged every delta naming one of the 19 center `c3` cell ids): exactly 20 deltas, **all `updateNode`** — pooling re-binds those slots (`data-field`, `aria-colindex`, `data-record-id`, `role`, cls, text); nothing is ever removed or moved.

So in the failing run, the center body's re-binding `updateNode`s never reached the main thread **for any row**, while the end body's render and the header's did. A whole body's render is missing while its vnode was adopted anyway.

**Reproduction recipe** (the only shape that has reproduced it; 0 of 136 without it):

```bash
npx playwright test \
  test/playwright/e2e/grid/CellEditingLockedBodies.spec.mjs \
  test/playwright/e2e/grid/CellEditingPooling.spec.mjs \
  test/playwright/e2e/grid/CellEditingTabSuspended.spec.mjs \
  -c test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs --repeat-each=25 --workers=12
```

ONE Playwright process. Two concurrent processes do **not** reproduce it (0 of 80) and corrupt each other's trace artifacts.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/grid/column/Base.mjs:166` — `afterSetLocked` calls `this.parent?.onColumnLockChange(this)`.
- `src/grid/Container.mjs:1056` — `async onColumnLockChange(column)`: re-sorts the columns, creates or updates the sub-grids, and passes sizes down.
- `src/grid/Body.mjs:738` — `createViewData(silent, force)`. Two early exits matter: the readiness guard (`store`, `availableRows`, `_containerWidth`, `columnPositions`, `mountedColumns[1]`) returns with **no retry**, while the `isVdomUpdating` branch re-registers itself through `Neo.manager.VDomUpdate.registerPreUpdate`. A lock change reaches `createViewData()` three times in the window the hold keeps `isEmbodied` false (#18865 / #18898 lineage).
- The dump says the readiness guard is not the explanation here: the center body has 37 fields and `mountedColumns [0,9]`, i.e. it *did* compute its new view data. The loss is between that and the DOM.

## The Mechanism — measured 2026-09-19, neither candidate A nor B

**The forced re-render is never requested.** The lock change asks `grid.Body#createViewData` for it, and the request is overwritten before it runs.

Reproduced **deterministically** at `dev@ab2e7cd17c`. A probe holds the center body's flight in the air for 300 ms, and `c3` is locked to the end during the hold. The census is `0/19/19` — `c3` renders in both the center and the end body, every time. The App Worker trail for the center body (probe on `createViewData`, `VDomUpdate.registerPreUpdate` / `executePreUpdates`, and every `updateBatch` flight):

| t (ms) | event |
|---|---|
| 486 | the lock change's `createViewData(false, true)` — **forced** — meets the held flight → deferred (`registerPreUpdate`) |
| 773 | the flight lands; the deferral runs and starts a new body flight |
| 778 | a second forced call is deferred, then an **unforced** `createViewData()` from the same lock change is deferred with `replaced: true` |
| 784 | the unforced call runs. It compares only `mountedColumns` (`[0,9]` before and after — a column leaving does not move the range), so it recycles every row |
| 786 | the center body's flight carries **0 deltas**. Nothing is ever queued again |

`VDomUpdate.registerPreUpdate` is a `Map.set` keyed by component id, so a later deferral **replaces** an earlier one. `grid.Body` is its only caller. Two deferrals made during one flight collapse into one run, and that run carries the *last* caller's arguments rather than the union of their intent: a forced request (re-bind the cells to the new column set) is dropped whenever a plain one follows it. The same holds for `silent`: a render request followed by a silent one would be dropped too.

This explains every piece of the original dump:
- the App Worker is settled (nothing in the air, nothing queued);
- `columnPositions` is already right (it is set before `createViewData`);
- the rows' cells are stale (they were never re-bound);
- the end body and the header are right (different components, their own flights).

## The Fix

`grid.Body#createViewData`'s deferral keeps the strongest intent across every deferral made during one flight. The deferred run is forced if any deferred call was forced, and renders (not silent) if any deferred call asked to render. The pending arguments live on the body and are consumed by the one run.

Rejected: making `registerPreUpdate` chain callbacks. It would run N re-renders where one suffices, and it moves a Body concern into the manager.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC-1**: the mechanism is named by measurement, with the head it ran at — the App Worker trail above (`dev@ab2e7cd17c`). The ticket as filed framed it as delta-stream candidates A or B; it is neither.
- [ ] **AC-2**: the fix lands in `grid.Body`'s deferral, with a deterministic e2e arm — a lock change that meets an in-flight center-body render — red on `dev` (`0/19/19`) and green with the fix. Plus a mutation that drops the force merge and reddens it.
- [ ] **AC-3**: the `lockEnd` arm of `CellEditingLockedBodies` survives the recipe. State the run count and the observed rate: the baseline is ~1 in 25 whole-recipe runs, so a green run of 25 is not evidence on its own, and the PR says how many it took.

## Out of Scope

- Rewriting the multi-body render path, or the `createViewData` readiness guard (the dump rules it out for this symptom).
- Making the stress recipe part of CI. It is a 12-worker reproduction harness, not a gate.
- The cell-editing behaviour around lock changes (#18865, #18885, #18898 delivered it); this ticket is about a render that goes missing underneath it.

## Avoided Traps

- ⛔ **Filing it as a flaky test.** The arm is not flaky: the App Worker is settled and correct, the DOM is wrong and final, and the user-visible result is a column rendered twice. A retry would hide it.
- ⛔ **Naming #18899 / #18901 as the cause because it smells like them.** Both merged before the head the dump was taken at. They are the family to look in, not the answer.
- ⛔ **Concluding from a passing run.** At ~1 in 25, "I could not reproduce it" is the expected outcome of a small sample.

## Related
